title: Charging Loop
statement: An electric shuttle runs a circular route through stations 0, 1, ..., n - 1 and back to 0. At station i it charges gain[i] units, then spends cost[i] units driving to the next station. It starts empty at a station of your choice and must complete one full lap without its charge dropping below zero at any point. Return the smallest starting station that works, or -1 if no station does.

examples.explanation: Starting at station 3 the charge goes 3, 6, 4, 2, 0 after each leg.
Total charge 9 is less than total cost 10, so no start works.

hints.content: If the total gain is less than the total cost, no start can work.
Simulating a lap from every start works but is quadratic.
Suppose you start at s and first run out of charge on the leg leaving station i. Then no station between s and i can work as a start either.
So when the running charge goes negative at i, jump the candidate start to i + 1 and reset the charge to 0.
If the total is non-negative, the last candidate start is a valid start, and it is the smallest one.

testCases.explanation: Starting at station 3 the charge goes 3, 6, 4, 2, 0 after each leg.
Total charge 9 is less than total cost 10, so no start works.
One station that exactly covers its own leg.
One station that cannot cover its leg.
Every start works; the smallest is 0.
Only the station with all the charge works.
Starting at 0: 3, 0, -1 fails. Starting at 3: 1, 4, 1, 0 completes the lap.
Totals balance exactly and station 0 works.

solutions.title: Simulate a lap from every station
solutions.intuition: Try each start in increasing order and return the first that survives a full lap.
solutions.approach: For each s, add gain - cost around the circle; abandon s as soon as the charge is negative.
solutions.pseudocode:
for s in 0..n-1: tank = 0; ok = true; for k in 0..n-1: i = (s+k) mod n; tank += gain[i] - cost[i]; if tank < 0: ok = false; break
  if ok: return s
return -1
commonMistakes: Checking the charge before adding the station's gain.
solutions.interviewExplanation: Trying each start in order returns the smallest valid one, but each lap costs O(n), so the whole thing is O(n²).

steps.title: Step 1
steps.content: Starts 0, 1 and 2 go negative on their first leg.

steps.title: Step 2
steps.content: Start 3: running charge 3, 6, 4, 2, 0, never negative. Return 3.

solutions.title: One-pass greedy reset
solutions.intuition: A start that fails at station i rules out every station between it and i, because each of those begins with less charge than the original start had at that point.
solutions.approach: Track total and tank. For each i, add gain[i] - cost[i] to both; if tank < 0, set start = i + 1 and tank = 0. Return start if total >= 0, otherwise -1.
solutions.pseudocode:
total = tank = start = 0
for i: d = gain[i] - cost[i]; total += d; tank += d; if tank < 0: start = i + 1; tank = 0
return total >= 0 ? start : -1
commonMistakes: Returning start without checking the total, which can return n or an invalid start.
Resetting start to i instead of i + 1.
solutions.interviewExplanation: If a run from s goes negative at i, every station between s and i starts with even less charge, so they all fail and I jump to i + 1. If the total balance is non-negative, the final candidate completes the lap, and because every earlier index was ruled out it's the smallest valid start. One pass, constant space.

steps.title: Step 1
steps.content: Deltas: -2, -2, -2, 3, 3. i=0: tank -2, start 1. i=1: start 2. i=2: start 3.

steps.title: Step 2
steps.content: i=3: tank 3; i=4: tank 6. The total is 0 >= 0, so return 3.
